must_haves: Dermatology skin images (clinical photographs or dermoscopy) of any skin condition, not limited to skin cancer
A skin tone label (Fitzpatrick type or Monk Skin Tone scale) attached to each image or each patient/case
A diagnosis label for each image or case
Fitzpatrick types V and VI (or the equivalent darkest tones) represented by more than a handful of images: on the order of a hundred or more, enough for a subgroup comparison
Publicly available dataset (no further access or licence constraint was stated by the researcher)

A.access_stated: Free registration and signed Research Use Agreement via Stanford AIMI portal; non-commercial, no redistribution
A.note: The DDI page says downloads require registering, which means agreeing to the Research Use Agreement, for 'personal, non-commercial research purposes only' and 'YOU MAY NOT SHARE THE DOWNLOAD LINK', and the AIMI page (https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/ddi-diverse-dermatology-images) lists 656 biopsy-confirmed images from 570 patients with 207 FST V-VI images (159 benign, 48 malignant), matching the answer; the pages do not say how long access takes, so 'minutes' is unverified.

A.access_stated: Open download from a public cloud bucket; SCIN Data Use Public License
A.note: The README says 'The data is stored in the dx-scin-public-data bucket on Google Cloud Storage' and the licence preamble names the 'SCIN Data Use Public License' (royalty-free, no re-identification); the paper (arXiv 2402.18545) gives V/VI only as percentages (self-reported 9.84%/6.57%, dermatologist-estimated 5.27%/0.57%, Monk 8-10 'less than 1.5%') and reports 'Fitzpatrick skin type: 2500, 49.65%' self-reporting, so per-case tone coverage and absolute V/VI counts cannot be confirmed from the documentation, and the answer's 'about 800' self-reported V/VI cases is not a figure stated in the documentation.
